contexts.text: Jehovah smote Pharaoh with great plagues () = that the scientifics were destroyed.
He smote them () = an avenging.
To smite = to destroy. AC 6765. AC 7580. AC 7603. AC 7606. AC 9552:end. AE 556:7.
Under Mother, see this reference.
To smite = to extinguish.
An Egyptian smiting a Hebrew () = an alienated Scientific endeavouring to destroy the truth of the Church.
He smote the Egyptian () = he destroyed the alienated Scientific.
To be smitten () = to be injured by falsities; for to be smitten, in the spiritual sense, = to be injured as to good and truth, that is, as to the things of the spiritual life.
Occurs. AC 7346. AC 7546. AC 8579. AR 828.
To smite = to remove.
To smite = damnation; for to smite is to kill or give to death, (which) = damnation. AC 7948.
Thou shalt smite the rook () = that they should urgently ask the Lord. To smite = to be urgent in asking, but from a humble heart; (but) he smote the rock from a hard heart.
To smite = to injure through falsity. AC 9015.
To smite = to injure; here, to weaken. AC 9029.
To smite = to ill-treat; for to smite is predicated of any kind of injury.
To smite = to injure.
To be smitten, when predicated of good and truth, = to be injured or harmed.

Jehovah smote the people () = the devastation of truth and good with them. To smite = to destroy; and to destroy, in the spiritual sense, is to deprive anyone of the truths and goods of faith and love, which in the Word is called desolation and vastation.
To smite the earth () = to bring ruin upon the Church.
Smitten with the axe () = rejected by those in falsities.
To smite = temptation. AE 654:9.
To smite, and kill = to be damned.
To be smitten, when predicated of goods and Knowledges, = to perish.
